advisory.finding: The pyproject-named pointer branch (`pyproject=(path.name == 'pyproject.toml')` reading `[tool.rebar.llm]`) in layer_llm_config_file is implemented but untested; every test in test_llm_config_pointer.py points at a *.toml file carrying a bare top-level [llm] table, so the pyproject extraction path (data['tool']['rebar']['llm']) has no coverage.
merged_from: No test covers the `pyproject.toml`-named pointer branch: `layer_llm_config_file` reads `[tool.rebar.llm]` (not top-level `[llm]`) when the pointed file is named `pyproject.toml` (`pyproject=(path.name == "pyproject.toml")`), an explicitly documented behavior. A regression that always read top-level `[llm]` would pass every existing test.

dropped.finding: No test covers a present-but-UNPARSEABLE pointed file. The design contract (per `_read_llm_file_table` docstring) is that the pointer layers OUTSIDE the malformed-config degrade and must fail loud (ConfigError from `_parse_toml`), never silently degrade to `{}`. Only the MISSING-path case is tested; a regression that wrapped `layer_llm_config_file` inside the degrade try/except would silently swallow a malformed pointed file with no failing test.
scenarios: CI supplies a REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE containing malformed TOML; the intended behavior is a loud ConfigError, but a degrade regression would silently ignore the file and run the checkout's config.
